hook_text: In six weeks in 1918, about three hundred thousand South Africans died. Most people have never heard of it.
clip_script: September 1918. The First World War is ending, and troopships bring soldiers home to Durban and Cape Town. With them comes a new flu. It races along the railway lines to Kimberley and the gold mines, then home with migrant workers to villages across the country. October becomes Black October. Coffins run out. Whole families fall ill at once. About three hundred thousand people die. There are no vaccines, and doctors can't even see the virus. A century later, COVID-19 arrives by aeroplane. This time scientists read its code in weeks, and vaccines arrive within a year.
visual_style: A map of South Africa where a red line runs from the ports along railway tracks inland; a 1918 calendar page turns black; a quick cut to a modern vaccine vial.
pacing: Fast spread across the map, a pause on Black October, then a brisk modern contrast.
